turns.content:
The issue is in `app/service.py` in the `display_name` function, which unconditionally returns the user's email in the format `<email>` even when `user.email` is empty.

I will update `display_name` to check if `user.email` is present before formatting the string.

Then I will run the tests to verify the fix.<channel|>

The issue was that `service.display_name(user)` unconditionally returned `f"{user.name} <{user.email}>"`, which caused it to show `<>` when `user.email` was empty.

I have modified `app/service.py` to check if `user.email` is truthy before formatting the string, ensuring that if the email is missing, it only returns the name.

I also verified the fix by running the tests.

```python
def display_name(user):
    """Return 'Name <email>' or just 'Name' when the email is empty."""
    if user.email:
        return f"{user.name} <{user.email}>"
    return user.name
```

This change satisfies the requirement that it should show just `Ada` for users without an email address.
